NKJV.1: Now these are the names of the children of Israel who came to Egypt; each man and his household came with Jacob:
NKJV.5: All those who were descendants of Jacob were seventy persons (for Joseph was in Egypt already).
NKJV.6: And Joseph died, all his brothers, and all that generation.
NKJV.7: But the children of Israel were fruitful and increased abundantly, multiplied and grew exceedingly mighty; and the land was filled with them.
NKJV.8: Now there arose a new king over Egypt, who did not know Joseph.
NKJV.9: And he said to his people, “Look, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we;

NKJV.18: So the king of Egypt called for the midwives and said to them, “Why have you done this thing, and saved the male children alive?”
NKJV.19: And the midwives said to Pharaoh, “Because the Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women; for they are lively and give birth before the midwives come to them.”
NKJV.20: Therefore God dealt well with the midwives, and the people multiplied and grew very mighty.
NKJV.21: And so it was, because the midwives feared God, that He provided households for them.
NKJV.22: So Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, “Every son who is born you shall cast into the river, and every daughter you shall save alive.”

NLT.1: These are the names of the sons of Israel (that is, Jacob) who moved to Egypt with their father, each with his family:
NLT.5: In all, Jacob had seventy descendants in Egypt, including Joseph, who was already there.
NLT.6: In time, Joseph and all of his brothers died, ending that entire generation.
NLT.7: But their descendants, the Israelites, had many children and grandchildren. In fact, they multiplied so greatly that they became extremely powerful and filled the land.
NLT.8: Eventually, a new king came to power in Egypt who knew nothing about Joseph or what he had done.
NLT.9: He said to his people, “Look, the people of Israel now outnumber us and are stronger than we are.
NLT.10: We must make a plan to keep them from growing even more. If we don’t, and if war breaks out, they will join our enemies and fight against us. Then they will escape from the country. ”
NLT.11: So the Egyptians made the Israelites their slaves. They appointed brutal slave drivers over them, hoping to wear them down with crushing labor. They forced them to build the cities of Pithom and Rameses as supply centers for the king.
NLT.12: But the more the Egyptians oppressed them, the more the Israelites multiplied and spread, and the more alarmed the Egyptians became.
NLT.13: So the Egyptians worked the people of Israel without mercy.
NLT.14: They made their lives bitter, forcing them to mix mortar and make bricks and do all the work in the fields. They were ruthless in all their demands.
NLT.15: Then Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, gave this order to the Hebrew midwives, Shiphrah and Puah:
NLT.16: “When you help the Hebrew women as they give birth, watch as they deliver. If the baby is a boy, kill him; if it is a girl, let her live.”
NLT.17: But because the midwives feared God, they refused to obey the king’s orders. They allowed the boys to live, too.
NLT.18: So the king of Egypt called for the midwives. “Why have you done this?” he demanded. “Why have you allowed the boys to live?”
NLT.19: “The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women,” the midwives replied. “They are more vigorous and have their babies so quickly that we cannot get there in time.”
NLT.20: So God was good to the midwives, and the Israelites continued to multiply, growing more and more powerful.
NLT.21: And because the midwives feared God, he gave them families of their own.
NLT.22: Then Pharaoh gave this order to all his people: “Throw every newborn Hebrew boy into the Nile River. But you may let the girls live.”

AMP.1: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel who came to Egypt with Jacob; each came with his household:
AMP.4: Dan and Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
AMP.5: All the descendants of Jacob were seventy people; Joseph was [already] in Egypt.
AMP.6: Then Joseph died, and all his brothers and all that generation,
AMP.7: but the Israelites were prolific and increased greatly; they multiplied and became extremely strong, so that the land was filled with them.
AMP.8: Now a new king arose over Egypt, who did not know Joseph [nor the history of his accomplishments].
AMP.9: He said to his people, "Behold, the people of the sons of Israel are too many and too mighty for us [they greatly outnumber us].
AMP.10: Come, let us deal shrewdly with them, so that they will not multiply and in the event of war, join our enemies, and fight against us and escape from the land."
AMP.11: So they set taskmasters over them to oppress them with hard labor. And the sons of Israel built Pithom and Raamses as storage cities for Pharaoh.
AMP.12: But the more the Egyptians oppressed them, the more they multiplied and expanded, so that the Egyptians dreaded and were exasperated by the Israelites.
AMP.13: And the Egyptians made the Israelites serve rigorously [forcing them into severe slavery].
AMP.14: They made their lives bitter with hard labor in mortar, brick, and all kinds of field work. All their labor was harsh and severe.
AMP.15: Then the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, one of whom was named Shiphrah (beauty) and the other named Puah (splendor),
AMP.16: "When you act as midwives to the Hebrew women and see them on the birthstool, if it is a son, you shall kill him; but if it is a daughter, she shall live."
AMP.17: But the midwives feared God [with profound reverence] and did not do as the king of Egypt commanded, but they let the boy babies live.
AMP.18: So the king of Egypt called for the midwives and said to them, "Why have you done this thing, and allowed the boy babies to live?"
AMP.19: The midwives answered Pharaoh, "Because the Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women; they are vigorous and give birth quickly and their babies are born before the midwife can get to them."
AMP.20: So God was good to the midwives, and the people [of Israel] multiplied and became very strong.
AMP.21: And because the midwives feared God [with profound reverence], He established families and households for them.
AMP.22: Then Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, "Every son who is born [to the Hebrews] must be thrown into the Nile, but every daughter you shall keep alive."

MSG.1: These are the names of the Israelites who went to Egypt with Jacob, each bringing his family members:
MSG.4: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
MSG.5: Seventy persons in all generated by Jacob's seed. Joseph was already in Egypt.
MSG.6: Then Joseph died, and all his brothers—that whole generation.
MSG.7: But the children of Israel kept on reproducing. They were very prolific—a population explosion in their own right—and the land was filled with them.
MSG.8: A new king came to power in Egypt who didn't know Joseph.
MSG.9: He spoke to his people in alarm, "There are way too many of these Israelites for us to handle.
MSG.10: We've got to do something: Let's devise a plan to contain them, lest if there's a war they should join our enemies, or just walk off and leave us."
MSG.11: So they organized them into work-gangs and put them to hard labor under gang-foremen. They built the storage cities Pithom and Rameses for Pharaoh.
MSG.12: But the harder the Egyptians worked them the more children the Israelites had—children everywhere! The Egyptians got so they couldn't stand the Israelites
MSG.13: and treated them worse than ever, crushing them with slave labor.
MSG.14: They made them miserable with hard labor—making bricks and mortar and back-breaking work in the fields. They piled on the work, crushing them under the cruel workload.
MSG.15: The king of Egypt had a talk with the two Hebrew midwives; one was named Shiphrah and the other Puah.
MSG.16: He said, "When you deliver the Hebrew women, look at the sex of the baby. If it's a boy, kill him; if it's a girl, let her live."
MSG.17: But the midwives had far too much respect for God and didn't do what the king of Egypt ordered; they let the boy babies live.
MSG.18: The king of Egypt called in the midwives. "Why didn't you obey my orders? You've let those babies live!"
MSG.19: The midwives answered Pharaoh, "The Hebrew women aren't like the Egyptian women; they're vigorous. Before the midwife can get there, they've already had the baby."
MSG.20: God was pleased with the midwives. The people continued to increase in number—a very strong people.
MSG.21: And because the midwives honored God, God gave them families of their own.
MSG.22: So Pharaoh issued a general order to all his people: "Every boy that is born, drown him in the Nile. But let the girls live."

NRSVCE.6: Then Joseph died, and all his brothers, and that whole generation.
NRSVCE.7: But the Israelites were fruitful and prolific; they multiplied and grew exceedingly strong, so that the land was filled with them.
NRSVCE.8: Now a new king arose over Egypt, who did not know Joseph.
NRSVCE.9: He said to his people, “Look, the Israelite people are more numerous and more powerful than we.
NRSVCE.10: Come, let us deal shrewdly with them, or they will increase and, in the event of war, join our enemies and fight against us and escape from the land.”
NRSVCE.11: Therefore they set taskmasters over them to oppress them with forced labor. They built supply cities, Pithom and Rameses, for Pharaoh.
NRSVCE.12: But the more they were oppressed, the more they multiplied and spread, so that the Egyptians came to dread the Israelites.
NRSVCE.13: The Egyptians became ruthless in imposing tasks on the Israelites,
NRSVCE.14: and made their lives bitter with hard service in mortar and brick and in every kind of field labor. They were ruthless in all the tasks that they imposed on them.
NRSVCE.15: The king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, one of whom was named Shiphrah and the other Puah,
NRSVCE.16: “When you act as midwives to the Hebrew women, and see them on the birthstool, if it is a boy, kill him; but if it is a girl, she shall live.”
NRSVCE.17: But the midwives feared God; they did not do as the king of Egypt commanded them, but they let the boys live.
NRSVCE.18: So the king of Egypt summoned the midwives and said to them, “Why have you done this, and allowed the boys to live?”
NRSVCE.19: The midwives said to Pharaoh, “Because the Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women; for they are vigorous and give birth before the midwife comes to them.”
NRSVCE.20: So God dealt well with the midwives; and the people multiplied and became very strong.
NRSVCE.21: And because the midwives feared God, he gave them families.
NRSVCE.22: Then Pharaoh commanded all his people, “Every boy that is born to the Hebrews you shall throw into the Nile, but you shall let every girl live.”

NET.1: These are the names of the sons of Israel who entered Egypt — each man with his household entered with Jacob:
NET.4: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
NET.5: All the people who were directly descended from Jacob numbered seventy. But Joseph was already in Egypt,
NET.6: and in time Joseph and his brothers and all that generation died.
NET.7: The Israelites, however, were fruitful, increased greatly, multiplied, and became extremely strong, so that the land was filled with them.
NET.8: Then a new king, who did not know about Joseph, came to power over Egypt.
NET.9: He said to his people, “Look at the Israelite people, more numerous and stronger than we are!
NET.10: Come, let’s deal wisely with them. Otherwise they will continue to multiply, and if a war breaks out, they will ally themselves with our enemies and fight against us and leave the country.”
NET.11: So they put foremen over the Israelites to oppress them with hard labor. As a result they built Pithom and Rameses as store cities for Pharaoh.
NET.12: But the more the Egyptians oppressed them, the more they multiplied and spread. As a result the Egyptians loathed the Israelites,
NET.13: and they made the Israelites serve rigorously.
NET.14: They made their lives bitter by hard service with mortar and bricks and by all kinds of service in the fields. Every kind of service the Israelites were required to give was rigorous.
NET.15: The king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, one of whom was named Shiphrah and the other Puah,
NET.16: “When you assist the Hebrew women in childbirth, observe at the delivery: If it is a son, kill him, but if it is a daughter, she may live.”
NET.17: But the midwives feared God and did not do what the king of Egypt had told them; they let the boys live.
NET.18: Then the king of Egypt summoned the midwives and said to them, “Why have you done this and let the boys live?”
NET.19: The midwives said to Pharaoh, “Because the Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women — for the Hebrew women are vigorous; they give birth before the midwife gets to them!”
NET.20: So God treated the midwives well, and the people multiplied and became very strong.
NET.21: And because the midwives feared God, he made households for them.
NET.22: Then Pharaoh commanded all his people, “All sons that are born you must throw into the river, but all daughters you may let live.”
